articles.title: Indonesia has not finalized how the state would take 70% of mining proceeds
articles.summary: Tempo reported on 23 November 2026 that Coordinating Minister Bahlil Lahadalia said the government has not finalized whether a proposed 70 percent state share of mining proceeds would be held through company shares or through revenue, and that existing contracts are being reviewed. He said the proposal is not final. The report said the Indonesian Nickel Industry Forum was still waiting for details, and that a 70:30 gross-split idea discussed earlier was not applied to coal and mineral mining.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury designates intermediaries it says sell Iranian oil
articles.summary: On 20 November 2026 the U.S. Treasury designated Mohammad Javad Bavand and Majid Taj under Executive Order 13902 for operating in Iran’s petroleum sector, and designated Mohammadhossein Servati and Mojtaba Arabnejad under Executive Order 13224. Treasury said Bavand and Taj are used to sell Iranian oil abroad and that, in many cases, the intermediaries have kept the oil revenue. It said property of the designated persons in the United States or held by U.S. persons is blocked unless authorized.

articles.title: Senegal’s president says he will implement 2026 budget changes by decree
articles.summary: Reuters, in a report published by CNBC Africa on 19 November 2026, said President Bassirou Diomaye Faye would implement changes to the 2026 budget by decree after parliament rejected them, and that lawmakers had also voted against a 2027 budget bill. The report said the bills are key to advancing an IMF staff-level agreement for a three-year $2.2 billion programme that still requires Executive Board approval, and that the government has agreed to rework its debt under the G20 Common Framework.

articles.title: Russia says strikes hit Odesa power substations, Chornomorsk port fuel storage and a cargo ship
articles.summary: Reuters, in a report published by Business Recorder on 19 November 2026, said Russia’s defence ministry reported overnight drone strikes on two power substations in the Odesa region, fuel-storage facilities at the port of Chornomorsk, and a cargo ship the ministry said was carrying dual-use goods to Odesa. The ministry also said a power substation in Sumy was struck.

articles.title: Canada Gazette publishes the relisting of 11 Iranian oil, nuclear, bank and insurance entities
articles.summary: The 18 November 2026 Canada Gazette published SOR/2026-234, registered on 5 November 2026, adding 11 entities to the Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations, including the National Iranian Oil Company, National Iranian Tanker Company, Bank Mellat, Bank Melli Iran, the Export Development Bank of Iran and Iran Insurance Company. The regulatory impact statement says the entities were listed in 2013, delisted in 2016, and are being relisted, and that the measures freeze assets they may hold in Canada and prohibit persons in Canada and Canadians abroad from making property available to them.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury designates a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash network
articles.summary: On 18 November 2026 the U.S. Treasury designated the Lebanon-based Wa Ta'awanu Association and members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash network it said moves funds from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force to Hizballah. The designated companies include Lebanon-based Gold Global Company and Türkiye-based Sankari Gold. Treasury said property of the designated persons in the United States or held by U.S. persons is blocked unless authorized.

articles.title: IMF staff and Egypt reach agreement on the final Extended Fund Facility review
articles.summary: The Middle East News Agency reported on 18 November 2026 that IMF staff and Egypt reached a staff-level agreement on the eighth and final Extended Fund Facility review and the third Resilience and Sustainability Facility review, subject to Executive Board approval. The report said approval would release about US$1.5 billion under the EFF and up to about US$0.8 billion under the RSF. It said the authorities had allowed the exchange rate to adjust after higher imports widened the current-account deficit, and that gross reserves remained above the IMF’s reserve-adequacy metric.

articles.title: Berne Union members underwrote US$2.9tn in the first half of 2026
articles.summary: Global Trade Review reported on 18 November 2026 that Berne Union members underwrote US$2.9 trillion of export-credit and investment-insurance risk in the first half of 2026. New medium- and long-term cover was US$125 billion, 26 percent higher than a year earlier, while short-term cover was about 5 percent higher; the Berne Union said political risk insurance continued a long-term decline because new cover was not replacing policies running off. Claims were US$4 billion in the first half, compared with US$3.4 billion a year earlier, and Export Development Canada’s Leah Gilbert Morris was chosen as Berne Union president for a two-year term.
